verdict.method_note: Judgments come from the supplied vector enlargements and nearest-neighbor magnifications only. I cannot sample numeric pixel values through image reading, so 'white' vs 'gray antialias' below is a visual-tone judgment from the magnified blocks, and is stated with confidence levels rather than as measurement. All coordinates are approximate, normalized to the 0..24 viewport, left/right relative to the whole icon.

clearance_location.where: Right / lower-right of the whole icon. The parent frame's right edge and bottom-right corner are cut away by an arc that follows the badge; clearance band runs vertically along approx x 12.5-15.5, y 9.5-22.5, and continues under the badge along the bottom.

ink_connection.verdict: Continuous whitespace separation in the vector render; no ink connection found.
ink_connection.raster_caveat: At 24px the band between frame and badge reads as one column of light-to-mid gray rather than clean white around y 12-16 — separation survives as a value contrast, not as paper. At 16px that column darkens further and I would not certify it as open.

shackle_opening.at_24: Partially visible: a small light aperture inside the lock body reads at roughly [16.5,14,2,2], but its tone looks gray rather than paper-white, so it is coverage, not a clean hole.
shackle_opening.at_16: Not resolved. The badge collapses to an 'A'-like glyph; I cannot distinguish shackle void from body notch. Abstain.

clearance_location.where: The only clearance is interior, on the upper-left flank of the badge, formed by the parent's white window field: approx x 14-18.5, y 11-15.5. There is no clearance on the icon's outer right or bottom - the badge runs into the card's filled corner.

ink_connection.verdict: Yes - ink connects. The badge body is contiguous with the parent card's bottom-right fill; no continuous whitespace encircles the badge.
ink_connection.confidence: high at vector scale; the merge is equally evident at 24px and 16px, where badge and corner form one mass.

shackle_opening.at_24: Marginal. A thin light arc traces the shackle at about [15.5,13,4,3], but it is narrow and partly gray.
shackle_opening.at_16: Not visible as an opening. Abstain on any claim of a resolved gap.

clearance_location.where: Right / lower-right of the whole icon, as a wide arc cut into the body panel: approx x 12.5-16.5, y 11.5-22.5. A second, unrelated horizontal gap separates the header band from the panel at about y 9-10.5, full width.

ink_connection.verdict: Continuous whitespace separation; no ink connection found at any of the three scales.
ink_connection.raster_caveat: At 24px the arc holds as near-white with gray shoulders. At 16px it thins to roughly one pixel of light gray along the diagonal near [13,15] - still legible as a break, but no longer clean paper.

shackle_opening.at_24: A light slot reads inside the badge near [16,15,2.5,1.5], but this may be a keyhole/slot rather than the shackle void; tone appears gray-to-white. Partial.

ranking_by_visible_separation_only.reason: Widest, most continuous clearance arc; the only one whose break survives legibly into 16px.
Geometrically separated, but the band is narrower and reads as gray at 24px; the frame's right edge is also heavily truncated, weakening the read.
No outer clearance at all - badge and parent share ink.

verdict.uncertainty: R over P is a moderate-confidence call and rests on arc width, which I estimated visually. Q's last place is high confidence, since ink continuity is structural and scale-independent. All shackle-opening findings at 16px are abstentions: the magnified blocks do not let me separate white from partial coverage at that size. No publication score is offered.

assessment.scope: three filled window examples; a diagnostic only
assessment.pixelCorrection: P native24 has gray 244 at (16,12) and white 255 at (16,13); the shackle is not exclusively gray coverage. Reviewer cannot certify pixel values.
